--- PART 1/3 ---

RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "We need produce only Python source defining strategy(history,rng). Need improve parent."
STRATEGY: Parent is a cooperative TFT-like policy with occasional probing; trace simulates iterated PD against 12 source strategies and designs an adaptive probe-and-exploit policy; changes include defecting after detecting forgiveness, retaliating on opponent D, and defecting in the last round.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the population, many strategies defect late (e.g., slot 6, 11 defect after n>90). So we should also defect late to avoid being exploited."
STRATEGY: The parent is a Tit-for-Tat-like policy with forgiveness and occasional probing/exploitation. The trace simulates it against population slots (always-C, TFT, forgiving strategies) and redesigns it with explicit history-derived stats (forgiveness/retaliation counts, consecutive defections, defection rates) to exploit unconditional cooperators more aggressively while breaking DD cycles.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent's fitness is 279.1." / "The parent also probes occasionally, so we are just more aggressive."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates initially, probes/exploits after cooperation streaks, forgives after opponent defections, and defects in the endgame. Simulated against TFT, always-defect, slot 8, slot 4, and always-C. Changed by making probing adaptive: 50% first probe after 5 consecutive C's, then 40%/20%/5% depending on forgiveness-vs-retaliation, with endgame defection at n>=99.
